log.msg: usage.json/usage.jsonl refresh skipped - not in this task's write fence (v/3/** and 2026-09-20/v3-axis-fix/** only); the mastermind keeps that snapshot current

measured cause on the real board (394-line board.jsonl, copied read-only to scratch-board.jsonl in this task dir - never touched the real file): 43 raw needs-you card lines / 68 focus lines before dedup; pinned_of() after dedup and filtering settled the strip at 25 distinct pinned cards. Before fix, driven headless: sticky box 713px of an 895px column at 1920 = 79.7 percent, matching the owner's own "eighty percent" exactly; at 400px the sticky box measured 1169px in a 461px column = 254 percent, meaning zero timeline pixels were ever reachable on a phone.

decision.topic: how many pinned cards to show collapsed
decision.chose: 4, ranked by the grid view's own weight() score (needs-you base, then mentions, then hits, then recency), with a plain "+N more" to expand and a CSS max-height:9em/overflow-y:auto backstop on .v3-pinned regardless of the JS count
decision.alternative: 3 felt stingy at 1920 (judged by eye per the brief) and a fixed pixel height alone, with no JS cap, would have silently hidden or truncated mid-card whichever needs-you items didn't fit - including possibly the newest urgent one, which is the one thing this strip exists to never bury. Rejected sorting by recency alone for the same reason: an old but still-unresolved needs-you card could get pushed out of the visible 4 by a newer, less important one.

log.msg: expand proof: clicking +21 more grew the box by only 62px (from 148px to ~210px including the hour/clock row) before the 9em cap took over; .v3-pinned then reported scrollHeight 647 > clientHeight 144, i.e. it scrolls internally instead of pushing .v3-axis-list (the timeline) down. This is the structural backstop working even though the JS cap already handles today's 23 needs-you cards - it is what keeps a future, bigger backlog from reopening this bug.

Live toggle proven headless, all four states: ON = classes "v3-live-btn on prim", background rgb(255,143,96), opacity 1, white text (the framework's own .prim utility, reused rather than re-declared - css skill, climb the ladder). OFF (manual click) = classes "v3-live-btn", background rgb(242,242,242), opacity 0.6, muted grey text. Scrolling .v3-inbox to scrollTop=120 (>24px threshold) while Live was on turned it off by itself (classes read back as plain "v3-live-btn", no "on"/"prim"). Clicking a card ("One page: start here, in order") while Live was on also turned it off by itself at the same moment the card became selected. All four driven with .claude/skills/ui-test/drive.mjs, not just described - screenshots and steps.json in the scratchpad, keeper pngs copied into this task's shots/ dir.

real files untouched, proven: md5 of public/framework/ai/verdicts.jsonl identical before and after this whole task (6cc15bd9...). public/framework/ai/board.jsonl DID change hash, but only because it is the live, shared, append-only activity log other minions post to constantly during this same session (it grew from 394 to 396 lines while this task ran) - diffed the first 394 lines against the scratch-board.jsonl snapshot taken at the start and they are byte-identical, so nothing this task did touched it; the two new lines are another minion's own cards (dictate-fix).

assign.outcome:
**Both fixes landed and proven headless.** The pinned strip (`.v3-axis-sticky`) went from **80% of the column at 1920px, 254% at 400px (no timeline reachable at all)** to **17% at 1920px, 39% at 400px** — capped two ways so a bigger backlog than today's 23 `needs-you` cards can't reopen this: a top-4 list ranked by the grid view's own `weight()` score, plus a `max-height`/`overflow-y:auto` backstop in the CSS itself. Live now shows a solid primary-orange fill when on and a dimmed, disabled-looking pill when off, and was actually driven — not just described — turning itself off on a real scroll past 24px and on a real card click.
